findings.title: Excel exports lack cell formatting
findings.description: Export classes do not implement WithHeadings, WithStyles, or WithColumnFormatting. Resulting .xlsx files have headers but they are not bold, have no background color, borders, or defined column widths. Data rows also lack styling.
findings.actionItem: Update WaterLevelExport, ConsumptionReadingExport, RestrictionExport, and ScheduledCutExport to implement WithStyles interface and add header formatting (bold, background color #1a5276, white text) and column width settings.

findings.title: Filter validation silently skips invalid values
findings.description: DroughtExportService uses when($value && array_key_exists($value, ConstantMap)) to conditionally apply filters. An invalid enum value is silently skipped rather than rejected or logged. Invalid filters produce unfiltered results indistinguishable from deliberate no-filter requests.
findings.actionItem: Add logging when filter validation fails, or consider throwing an exception for invalid enum values instead of silently skipping them.

findings.title: Empty result sets are not distinguished from populated ones
findings.description: PDF templates display 'Aucune donnée disponible' in the @empty fallback. Excel exports produce a valid .xlsx file with headers and no data rows. Neither returns a warning status or HTTP header indicating the export is empty. Files are downloaded normally.
findings.actionItem: Consider logging when exports are empty, or optionally displaying a UI toast/notification to inform the user that no data matched their filters.

findings.title: No per-zone authorization in export endpoints
findings.description: Export methods do not verify that the requesting user has permission to access the data being exported. A manager restricted to zones A and B can request an export of zone C's data by crafting the URL with zone_id=3.
findings.actionItem: Add per-zone authorization checks in export methods using $this->authorize() or a gate, matching any existing zone-level access control patterns in the application. Check if zone-scoped access is already enforced elsewhere in the back office.
